title: Rabbi Chiyya son of Rabbi Shabtai
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Hyman identifies Rabbi Akiva at the end of Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot, chapter 2, as an Amora speaking in his name. Hyman cites Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin, chapter 5, halakhah 1, folio 27b, for the question of Rabbi Chiyya son of Rabbi Shivtai: “How did they go out to the study house of Moses?” etc.

notes.text: ב״מד denotes a study house, בית המדרש, rather than a court, בית דין. The supplied quotation spells the father שיבתיי, Shivtai, while the heading has Shabtai; both forms are retained. The cited Sanhedrin occurrence remains unverified in the returned research, and the historical 27b is not mapped onto the Bavli.

Hyman’s printed reference is Sanhedrin 5:1, folio 27b (vol. II, p. 449). The question occurs in Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin 5:1 (Vilna 32b), in a discussion of the limits of the wilderness camp. The Wikisource text reads Shivtai (שיבתיי), while Guggenheimer’s Hebrew reads Shuvtai (שובתיי). At Yevamot 2:12 the words “Rabbi Akiva said” precede Chiyya son of Rabbi Shabtai’s objection, which Rabbi Yose answers. The description of Akiva as an Amora speaking in Chiyya’s name follows Hyman’s reading.
